newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixed firmer but market marks time.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixed firmer but market marks time.

text.p: Precious metals prices added modestly to Friday's gains on Monday afternoon as the markets watched the dollar, the U.S. stock market and the bond market for further falls, traders said.
Business had been slow during the European morning as dealers waited the start of U.S. trading to determine whether or not the rally would continue.
"It is not entirely clear whether this was short covering or there was some fresh buying coming into gold on Friday," one analyst said.
Gold was fixed at $327.70 per ounce up from $326.20 on Monday morning and against $323.70 on Friday.
At the fixing the New York Comex December contract was $1.50 ahead at $321.90 but volume was light and attention was on the foreign exchange markets and the stock exchange for directional hints.

"What was happening elsewhere played a major role in the gold market on Friday," said one market participant, referring to the 156-point fall in the Dow and the losses sustained by the dollar and the U.S. long bond.
"If there is a reallocation of funds going on (from the stock markets into gold and elsewhere) it is difficult to know what these people's targets in gold would be," a dealer said.
He added that whereas a sharp moves in the gold price would not be surprising, the market was locking into a $321.00-$328.00 for the time being, another dealer said.
Further out the upside looked limited to $340.00. More immediately, $327.00-$328.00 could prove tempting numbers at which to take profits.
Silver was three cents firmer at $4.43/$4.45 and was quietly consolidating after fairly wide fluctuations last week.
The arrival of Russian platinum and palladium in Tokyo on Friday took very little of the heat out of the PGM (platinum group metals) markets.
"A major concern is the size of the short positions on Tocom (Tokyo's precious metals futures market)," said one dealer.
Russia was out of the market as a supplier of platinum and palladium through the first six months of this year as it adjusted to a series of personnel and administrative changes.
Platinum was quoted at $444.80/$447.80, wiping out earlier modest losses to be $2.80 ahead and palladium was up $1.25 at $234.00/$237.00.
